scaling_method.application_point: after loading the feasible checkpoint and opening the eight optimization degrees of freedom

experiments.conclusion: Modern autoscaling prevents the catastrophic first step and reduces the scaled dual infeasibility, but does not converge in ten iterations.
The solve remains close to its feasible costed start but makes insufficient optimization progress.
The autoscaled solve remains near the published optimum and is much more stable than inherited/default scaling, but it does not satisfy the requested IPOPT convergence gate in 100 iterations.

legacy_scaling_defect: The existing Arc loop in set_scaling_factors references the final unit-loop variable instead of the Arc being traversed, so it does not apply the intended equality-constraint scaling to expanded Arc constraints.
conclusion: IDAES 2.12 AutoScaler materially stabilizes the optimization, but does not yet provide a reliable converged reproduction. Further work should isolate the remaining dual infeasibility and test a corrected modular scaling policy rather than declaring the near-published iterate reproduced.
